evals.name: resume-seeds-the-rework-dir
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the Asana task, finds no PR URL in its notes, stories or attachments, and treats the task name and notes as the reported issue. It resolves the prior run from .harness/*/manifest.json, cds to that worktree, creates .harness/<SPEC_NAME>-rework-1, copies baseline.json and claims.json into it, removes .harness/current-phase, reproduces the reported bug as a failing test, then invokes orchestrate at entry stage coder.
expectations: Resolves PRS from the Asana task before searching for SPEC_NAME
Treats the empty PRS list as the QA case rather than halting
Finds SPEC_NAME by searching .harness/*/manifest.json rather than guessing from the ticket id
Creates a sibling rework spec dir named <SPEC_NAME>-rework-<N>, not a subdirectory of the original
Copies baseline.json and claims.json into the rework spec dir
Runs rm -f .harness/current-phase before dispatching any sub-agent
Writes a failing test reproducing the reported issue before making the fix
Invokes orchestrate with entry stage coder and the existing WORKTREE_PATH
anti_expectations: Does not create a new worktree
Does not write a design doc or a plan
Does not ask the user any question
Does not re-run the full pipeline from stage 0
Does not copy plan.md into the rework spec dir
Does not halt because the Asana task links no PR

evals.name: pr-comments-every-item-dispositioned
evals.expected_output: The skill fetches the PR's inline comments and review summaries, dispatches a general-purpose subagent to read the code at each path:line, gives each comment a verdict, and every fetched comment ends on exactly one disposition. The only file written is rework-report.html.
expectations: Derives repository acme/lydia and pr_number 214 from the URL, then fetches inline comments via the pulls/{N}/comments endpoint and review summaries via pulls/{N}/reviews
Dispatches a general-purpose subagent to read the code at each comment's path:line rather than reading the files itself
Assigns every comment one of: valid, stale, out-of-scope, wrong
A 'wrong' verdict names the behavior that makes the existing code correct
Writes rework-report.html covering, per comment: what the reviewer said, the verdict, what changed, and why
Every fetched comment id ends on exactly one disposition: applied, deferred, or dropped
Writes exactly one file: rework-report.html
anti_expectations: Does not pause to ask which comments to accept
Does not silently skip a comment it decided not to act on
Does not treat its own findings as review feedback — the items come from the human reviewer

evals.name: blast-radius-fails-open
evals.prompt: The rework fix touched packages/api/src/mailer.ts and packages/api/src/config.ts. mailer.ts is named in phases/phase-2.md; config.ts is named in no phase file. Trace the blast radius.
evals.expected_output: A general-purpose subagent traces the radius and returns two lists. Because config.ts maps to no phase, the radius widens to every coverage id in the prior proof-report. The in-radius list is passed in the Stage 5 dispatch as functional-verify's requirement enumeration. The out-of-radius list reaches rework-report.html as a caveat, and only when something was not re-verified.
expectations: Dispatches a general-purpose subagent for the trace instead of reading the phase files itself
Derives changed files from git diff against the pre-rework sha
Maps changed files to phases by searching the original run's phases/phase-*.md
Widens the radius to the full prior coverage set because config.ts maps to no phase
Carries each in-radius id's requirement text from the original plan.md
Passes the in-radius list in the Stage 5 dispatch prompt as the requirement enumeration
Every coverage id from the prior report appears in either the in-radius or out-of-radius list
Each out-of-radius id carries the reason it is out
anti_expectations: Does not write a scope file — the dispatch prompt carries the in-radius list, and the report carries the out-of-radius list as a caveat
Does not narrow scope when a changed file maps to no phase
Does not omit ids from both lists
Does not edit functional-verify's own scope rule or claim a partial verification is complete

evals.name: asana-task-fans-out-to-every-linked-pr
evals.expected_output: The Asana task links two PRs, acme/lydia#25 and acme/serana#24. The skill fetches comments from both, triages every comment from both, and every fetched comment ends on exactly one disposition. Each report item sourceHref points at the repository and PR that comment came from.
expectations: Collects both PR URLs from the Asana task rather than stopping at the first
Runs the comments and reviews fetch once per PR, with that PR's repository and pr_number
Identifies a comment by repository, pr_number and id together, not by id alone
Resolves a single SPEC_NAME covering both PRs
Builds each sourceHref from that comment's own repository and pr_number
Every fetched comment across both PRs ends on exactly one disposition
anti_expectations: Does not triage only one of the two PRs
Does not create a separate rework spec dir per PR
Does not ask the user which PR to use
